proofs.proof_tex:
Because \(A\) and \(B\) are normalized nonnegative probability tables, their row sums and selected cells satisfy
\[
0\le p\le1,\qquad 0\le r\le1,\qquad 0\le a\le p,\qquad 0\le b\le r.
\]
Consequently every \(w_{ij}\) is nonnegative, and
\[
p=w00+w01,\qquad r=w00+w10.
\]

First suppose \(MC(A,B)\ne\varnothing\), and choose \(M\in MC(A,B)\).  By \(\text{lem:four-stratum-reduction}\), the mass \(c=s(0,0)\) of this model satisfies \(cL\le c\le cU\).  Hence \(cL\le cU\).

Conversely, suppose \(cL\le cU\).  Set \(c=cL\) and \(d=0\).  The definition of \(F(A,B)\) gives \(cL\le c\le cU\).  Moreover,
\[
0\le d=0\le w11=(1-p)(1-r),
\]
where the last inequality uses only \(p,r\in[0,1]\); it remains valid when \(w11=0\).  Thus \((cL,0)\in F(A,B)\).  The closed-simplex source-preserving lift \(\text{thm:source-preserving-lift-closed-simplex}\) then constructs an \(M\in MC(A,B)\).  We have proved
\[
MC(A,B)\ne\varnothing\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad cL\le cU.
\]

It remains to simplify the latter condition without any strict inequality.  Since
\[
cL=\max\{0,a-w01,b-w10\},\qquad cU=\min\{w00,a,b\},
\]
the inequality \(cL\le cU\) is equivalent to requiring that each of the three lower candidates be at most each of the three upper candidates.  The comparisons involving the lower candidate \(0\) hold because \(w00,a,b\ge0\).  For the lower candidate \(a-w01\),
\[
a-w01\le w00
\]
follows from \(a\le p=w00+w01\), and \(a-w01\le a\) follows from \(w01\ge0\).  Its only remaining comparison is \(a-w01\le b\).  Similarly,
\[
b-w10\le w00
\]
follows from \(b\le r=w00+w10\), and \(b-w10\le b\) follows from \(w10\ge0\); its only remaining comparison is \(b-w10\le a\).  Therefore
\[
\begin{aligned}
cL\le cU
&\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad a-w01\le b\ \text{ and }\ b-w10\le a\\
&\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad -w10\le a-b\le w01\\
&\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad -(1-p)r\le a-b\le p(1-r).
\end{aligned}
\]
Every step used weak inequalities only, so this equivalence covers \(p,r\in\{0,1\}\) and all equality cases.

Assume that all cells of the normalized tables \(A\) and \(B\) are rational and that \(MC(A,B)\ne\varnothing\).  Then \(p,r,a,b\), the four products \(w_{ij}\), and the max--min quantities \(cL,cU\) are rational.  By \(\text{thm:sharp-risk-interval}\), the lower endpoint is attained at
\[
(c,d)=(cU,0),
\]
and the upper endpoint is attained at
\[
(c,d)=(cL,w11).
\]
Compatibility gives \(cL\le cU\), and \(w11\ge0\), so both displayed pairs belong to \(F(A,B)\).

For either endpoint pair, put
\[
(n_{00},n_{01},n_{10},n_{11}):=(c,a-c,b-c,d).
\]
Define, branch by branch,
\[
t_{ij}:=
\begin{cases}
n_{ij}/w_{ij},&w_{ij}>0,\\
0,&w_{ij}=0,
\end{cases}
\qquad (i,j)\in D^2,
\]
and
\[
\gamma_A:=
\begin{cases}
A(1,1)/(1-p),&1-p>0,\\
0,&1-p=0,
\end{cases}
\qquad
\gamma_B:=
\begin{cases}
B(1,1)/(1-r),&1-r>0,\\
0,&1-r=0.
\end{cases}
\]
Every numerator and every positive denominator in these formulas is rational.  Division of two rationals by a nonzero rational is rational, and each zero branch equals the rational number \(0\).  Hence all \(t_{ij},\gamma_A,\gamma_B\) are rational, including on every support face.

The closed-simplex lift \(\text{thm:source-preserving-lift-closed-simplex}\) forms the distinct ordered thresholds from
\[
\{t_{00},t_{01},t_{10},t_{11},\gamma_A,\gamma_B,1/2,0,1\}.
\]
There are at most nine distinct listed values, hence at most eight successive differences.  Because every threshold is rational, every private-root mass \(\lambda_k-\lambda_{k-1}\) is rational.  The binary-source masses \(p,1-p,r,1-r\) are rational as well, while \(fX,fZ,fY\) are deterministic.  The lift therefore supplies rational-weight endpoint models with \(|\operatorname{supp}(W0)|\le8\).

Each source root has at most two support points.  Thus the number of exogenous assignments with labels retained is at most
\[
2\cdot2\cdot8=32.
\]
Enumerating these assignments, multiplying their rational product weights, applying the deterministic structural functions under \(\operatorname{do}(Z=0)\), \(\operatorname{do}(X=0)\), and \(\operatorname{do}(X=0,Z=0)\), and summing verifies all eight supplied cells and the relevant endpoint exactly.  This proves the claimed rational certificates even when one or both source roots are degenerate.

added_lemmas.statement: For every pair \((A,B)\) of normalized nonnegative \(2\times2\) probability tables for which \(F(A,B)\ne\varnothing\), and every \((c,d)\in F(A,B)\), the handle \(Hthr\) constructs a finite model \(M\in MC(A,B)\) with binary-valued roots \(U0,V0\) (possibly degenerate), a private root \(W0\) with at most eight support points, mutually independent roots, and one deterministic outcome function \(fY\) shared by all regimes, such that \(q=a+b-c+d\).  The construction reproduces all four cells of \(A\) and all four cells of \(B\).
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Fix normalized nonnegative \(2\times2\) probability tables \(A,B\) and a pair \((c,d)\in F(A,B)\).  Normalization and nonnegativity imply
\[
0\le p,r\le1,\qquad 0\le a\le p,\qquad 0\le b\le r.
\]
Let
\[
(n_{00},n_{01},n_{10},n_{11}):=(c,a-c,b-c,d).
\]
Membership in \(F(A,B)\) means
\[
\max\{0,a-w01,b-w10\}\le c\le\min\{w00,a,b\},
\qquad 0\le d\le w11.
\]
It follows, term by term, that
\[
0\le n_{00}\le w00,qquad
0\le n_{01}\le w01,qquad
0\le n_{10}\le w10,qquad
0\le n_{11}\le w11.
\]
For example, \(n_{01}\ge0\) follows from \(c\le a\), while \(n_{01}\le w01\) follows from \(c\ge a-w01\); the argument for \(n_{10}\) is symmetric.  In particular,
\[
w_{ij}=0\quad\Longrightarrow\quad n_{ij}=0.
\]
Define
\[
t_{ij}:=
\begin{cases}
n_{ij}/w_{ij},&w_{ij}>0,\\
0,&w_{ij}=0.
\end{cases}
\]
The displayed mass inequalities prove \(0\le t_{ij}\le1\), and the two branches jointly give the identity
\[
w_{ij}t_{ij}=n_{ij}
\]
for every \((i,j)\in D^2\).

Define the remaining two response probabilities by
\[
\gamma_A:=
\begin{cases}
A(1,1)/(1-p),&1-p>0,\\
0,&1-p=0,
\end{cases}
\qquad
\gamma_B:=
\begin{cases}
B(1,1)/(1-r),&1-r>0,\\
0,&1-r=0.
\end{cases}
\]
If \(1-p>0\), then normalization and nonnegativity give
\[
0\le A(1,1)\le A(1,0)+A(1,1)=1-p,
\]
so \(0\le\gamma_A\le1\).  If \(1-p=0\), the same row-sum identity forces \(A(1,0)=A(1,1)=0\), and hence the chosen value \(\gamma_A=0\) satisfies
\[
(1-p)\gamma_A=A(1,1).
\]
The positive-denominator branch satisfies this identity by cancellation.  Thus it holds in both branches.  The identical argument for the second table proves \(0\le\gamma_B\le1\) and
\[
(1-r)\gamma_B=B(1,1).
\]

Let \(U0,V0\) be independent \(D\)-valued roots with
\[
\mathbb P(U0=0)=p,
\qquad
\mathbb P(V0=0)=r,
\]
and set \(fX(u)=u\), \(fZ(v)=v\).  Degenerate laws at \(p\in\{0,1\}\) or \(r\in\{0,1\}\) are allowed.  For \((x,z,u,v)\in D^4\), prescribe
\[
h(x,z,u,v):=
\begin{cases}
t_{uv},&(x,z)=(0,0),\\
\gamma_A,&(x,z)=(1,0),\\
\gamma_B,&(x,z)=(0,1),\\
1/2,&(x,z)=(1,1).
\end{cases}
\]
The set
\[
\mathcal H:=\{t_{00},t_{01},t_{10},t_{11},\gamma_A,\gamma_B,1/2\}
\]
contains at most seven values, all in \([0,1]\).  List the distinct elements of \(\mathcal H\cup\{0,1\}\) as
\[
0=\lambda_0<\lambda_1<\cdots<\lambda_m=1.
\]
There are at most nine listed values, so \(m\le8\).  Independently of \((U0,V0)\), let \(W0\) take values \(1,\ldots,m\) with
\[
\mathbb P(W0=k)=\lambda_k-\lambda_{k-1},
\qquad 1\le k\le m.
\]
These masses are positive by distinctness and sum to \(1\) by telescoping.  Define
\[
g(h,k):=\mathbf 1\{\lambda_k\le h\}.
\]
For every \(h=\lambda_j\in\mathcal H\), including \(j=0\) and \(j=m\),
\[
\mathbb P\{g(h,W0)=1\}
=\sum_{k=1}^{j}(\lambda_k-\lambda_{k-1})
=\lambda_j=h,
\]
with the sum understood as empty when \(j=0\).  Now define the single deterministic structural function
\[
fY(x,z,u,v,k):=g(h(x,z,u,v),k).
\]
The product law makes \(U0,V0,W0\) mutually independent, and this same \(fY\) is used under every intervention.

We verify the complete experimental tables.  Under \(\operatorname{do}(Z=0)\), the threshold identity and the branchwise identities \(w_{ij}t_{ij}=n_{ij}\) give
\[
\begin{aligned}
\mathbb P_M(X=0,Y=1\mid\operatorname{do}(Z=0))
&=w00t_{00}+w01t_{01}=n_{00}+n_{01}=a=A(0,1),\\
\mathbb P_M(X=1,Y=1\mid\operatorname{do}(Z=0))
&=(1-p)\gamma_A=A(1,1).
\end{aligned}
\]
Since the two \(X\)-row masses are \(p\) and \(1-p\), normalization yields
\[
\begin{aligned}
\mathbb P_M(X=0,Y=0\mid\operatorname{do}(Z=0))&=p-a=A(0,0),\\
\mathbb P_M(X=1,Y=0\mid\operatorname{do}(Z=0))&=1-p-A(1,1)=A(1,0).
\end{aligned}
\]
Under \(\operatorname{do}(X=0)\), the symmetric calculation gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
\mathbb P_M(Z=0,Y=1\mid\operatorname{do}(X=0))
&=w00t_{00}+w10t_{10}=n_{00}+n_{10}=b=B(0,1),\\
\mathbb P_M(Z=1,Y=1\mid\operatorname{do}(X=0))
&=(1-r)\gamma_B=B(1,1),\\
\mathbb P_M(Z=0,Y=0\mid\operatorname{do}(X=0))&=r-b=B(0,0),\\
\mathbb P_M(Z=1,Y=0\mid\operatorname{do}(X=0))&=1-r-B(1,1)=B(1,0).
\end{aligned}
\]
Thus all eight cells agree exactly, including null rows, and the constructed model belongs to \(MC(A,B)\).

Finally, under \(\operatorname{do}(X=0,Z=0)\),
\[
\begin{aligned}
q
&=\sum_{i,j\in D}\mathbb P(U0=i,V0=j)t_{ij}\\
&=\sum_{i,j\in D}w_{ij}t_{ij}\\
&=n_{00}+n_{01}+n_{10}+n_{11}\\
&=c+(a-c)+(b-c)+d=a+b-c+d.
\end{aligned}
\]
This proves the construction and its support bound on the entire closed simplex.

For the prescribed kill test,
\[
A=((1/8,3/8),(3/8,1/8)),
\qquad
B=((3/8,1/8),(3/8,1/8)),
\]
one has \(p=r=1/2\), \(a=3/8\), \(b=1/8\), and \(cL=cU=1/8\).  Both endpoint models use independent fair \(U0,V0\),
\[
(t_{00},t_{01},t_{10})=(1/2,1,0),
\qquad
\gamma_A=\gamma_B=1/4,
\]
with \(t_{11}=0\) at the lower endpoint and \(t_{11}=1\) at the upper endpoint.  The ordered threshold set is \(\{0,1/4,1/2,1\}\), so \(W0\) has masses \(1/4,1/4,1/2\).  Direct substitution into the preceding eight cell identities recovers exactly the displayed \(A\) and \(B\), while
\[
q=\frac14\left(\frac12+1+0+t_{11}\right)
\]
equals \(3/8\) and \(5/8\), respectively.
added_lemmas.justification: The common threshold construction lifts every feasible mass pair on the closed probability simplex without coupling the two source roots.
added_lemmas.gap: Generic finite canonicalization does not itself give the eight-point source-preserving certificate with explicit null-stratum branches.
added_lemmas.consumer: This theorem supplies common-SCM attainment for compatibility, sharpness, exact endpoint certificates, and the fixed-graph analytic dispatch.

proposed.name: Hthr
proposed.construction: Source-preserving threshold-extension handle on normalized nonnegative tables: for \((c,d)\in F(A,B)\), set \((n_{00},n_{01},n_{10},n_{11})=(c,a-c,b-c,d)\), define \(t_{ij}=n_{ij}/w_{ij}\) when \(w_{ij}>0\) and \(t_{ij}=0\) when \(w_{ij}=0\), define \(\gamma_A=A(1,1)/(1-p)\) when \(1-p>0\) and \(\gamma_A=0\) when \(1-p=0\), and define \(\gamma_B=B(1,1)/(1-r)\) when \(1-r>0\) and \(\gamma_B=0\) when \(1-r=0\).  Use response probability \(t_{uv}\) at \((x,z)=(0,0)\), \(\gamma_A\) at \((x,z)=(1,0)\), \(\gamma_B\) at \((x,z)=(0,1)\), and \(1/2\) at \((x,z)=(1,1)\).  Order the distinct values of these probabilities together with \(0,1\); successive threshold gaps are the atom masses of one private root \(W0\), and threshold indicators define one deterministic map \(fY\) for every regime while \(U0\) and \(V0\) retain their independent source laws.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The construction must define all response probabilities on zero-mass strata and null observed rows rather than divide by zero.

proposed.name: Cert
proposed.construction: On input normalized nonnegative tables \((A,B)\), compute \((p,r,a,b)\), return incompatible exactly when either \(a-b<-(1-p)r\) or \(a-b>p(1-r)\), and otherwise return \((qL,qU)\) from their three-branch formulas.  If all input cells are rational and the pair is compatible, also use \((c,d)=(cU,0)\) and \((c,d)=(cL,w11)\).  For either pair set \((n_{00},n_{01},n_{10},n_{11})=(c,a-c,b-c,d)\), compute \(t_{ij}=n_{ij}/w_{ij}\) when \(w_{ij}>0\) and set \(t_{ij}=0\) when \(w_{ij}=0\); compute \(\gamma_A=A(1,1)/(1-p)\) when \(1-p>0\) and set \(\gamma_A=0\) when \(1-p=0\); compute \(\gamma_B=B(1,1)/(1-r)\) when \(1-r>0\) and set \(\gamma_B=0\) when \(1-r=0\).  Use response probabilities \(t_{uv}\) when \((x,z)=(0,0)\), \(\gamma_A\) when \((x,z)=(1,0)\), \(\gamma_B\) when \((x,z)=(0,1)\), and \(1/2\) when \((x,z)=(1,1)\).  Sort the distinct elements of these probabilities together with \(\{0,1\}\) as \(0=\lambda_0<\cdots<\lambda_m=1\), give \(W0=k\) mass \(\lambda_k-\lambda_{k-1}\), take independent binary-valued \(U0,V0\) with zero-probabilities \(p,r\), set \(fX(u)=u\), \(fZ(v)=v\), and set \(fY(x,z,u,v,k)=\mathbf 1\{\lambda_k\le h(x,z,u,v)\}\) for the specified response probability \(h\).  Emit the resulting two models in \(MC(A,B)\) as lower- and upper-endpoint certificates.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The constant-size certificate algorithm needs explicit zero-denominator branches on the closed simplex.
The old statement explicitly restricted the lift to strictly positive tables; the proved replacement has the same conclusion for all normalized nonnegative tables and migrates every downstream use.

prose_updates.tldr: For two complete experiments on the binary collider with two independent shared roots and private outcome noise, arbitrary normalized tables \(A,B\), including structural zeros, are compatible exactly when \(-(1-p)r\le a-b\le p(1-r)\).  When compatible, the all-zero joint-intervention risk has the sharp closed interval \([\max\{a,b,a+b-pr\},\min\{a+1-p,b+1-r,a+b+(1-p)(1-r)\}]\).  One common deterministic outcome law with independent binary-valued source roots and at most eight private-root atoms attains every real interval point; rational inputs have exact rational endpoint certificates, yielding a constant-time fixed-graph procedure and an optional conservative outer sampling interval.

project_justification.gap: General discrete-SCM methods can optimize this query sharply by a polynomial program, and causal-marginal methods explain why overlapping reports must be compatible, but the checked literature does not supply this graph-specific closed-simplex frontier, its analytic endpoints, or the small common-SCM witness.
project_justification.niche: For this fixed binary collider and intervention menu, four natural-treatment strata expose the exact obstruction, while the product law of the two latent sources rules out unrestricted latent coupling and must be retained in every attaining model.
project_justification.fill: The paper proves the closed-simplex two-mass fiber, its source-preserving finite extension with explicit null-stratum branches, the resulting iff test and max--min sharp interval, and exact endpoint certificates.  This is an analytic specialization for the same fixed input handled by Autobounds, not a new general bounding compiler.

prose_updates.related_work: Duarte et al., JASA 2024, prove sharp finite-discrete causal bounds through generic polynomial programs with product disturbance probabilities and observational or experimental constraints, and implement that workflow in Autobounds.  Their theorem covers supplied categorical laws without a strict-positivity restriction; the present binary two-source collider is therefore a same-input closed-simplex specialization.  What is new here is not generic sharpness, but the derived compatibility inequality, closed-form endpoint map, and at-most-eight-atom common-SCM certificates that replace generic optimization for this one menu.  Zhang, Tian, and Bareinboim prove finite canonical SCM sufficiency for categorical counterfactual distributions, but their general reduction does not yield this source-preserving certificate size or these formulas.  Gresele et al. study compatibility of overlapping causal marginals, while Sachs et al. and Finkelstein and Shpitser provide neighboring response-function and logical-bound machinery; none of the checked statements gives this collider result.  Zaffalon et al., IJAR 2023, fuse observational, biased, and randomized sources to obtain approximate counterfactual ranges, making their work adjacent multi-source bounding rather than an exact theorem-level comparator.  Autobounds is the concrete software consumer: for this fixed graph, tables, and all-zero intervention query, the analytic certificate can serve as a special-case dispatch and regression oracle.  No package modification or runtime benchmark is claimed.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: The source-preserving step is now constructive on every support face: feasibility forces a zero success numerator whenever its stratum mass is zero, and null observed rows use explicit arbitrary response values.  The proof uses one common deterministic \(fY\), one private threshold root \(W0\), and mutually independent, possibly degenerate, source roots \(U0,V0\), and it verifies all eight experimental cells.  The product-source restriction remains load-bearing: a correlated source model can escape the interval.  The at-most-eight support count is sufficient, not proved minimal, and the optional sampling interval is conservative rather than tie-optimal.
prose_updates.honest_scope: The result covers arbitrary normalized binary \(2\times2\) experimental tables, including structural zeros and \(p,r\in\{0,1\}\), for the fixed collider, the two stated intervention tables, mutually independent source roots, private outcome noise, and the single risk \(P_M(Y=1\mid\operatorname{do}(X=0,Z=0))\).  Correlated or dependence-budget sources, different study populations, a simultaneous region for all four joint-intervention risks, three or more parents, an optimal-support theorem, tie-optimal inference, a general thicket compiler, and any field-tier claim remain excluded.  For compatible inputs, the interior width observation \(qU-qL\ge w11>0\) is asserted only when \(0<p,r<1\); boundary faces may have \(w11=0\) and can point-identify the risk.
